newsitem.title: UK: BA gets further payout from USAir.
newsitem.headline: BA gets further payout from USAir.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Tuesday it had received last month a further backpayment of dividends owed on its $400 million investment in preferred convertible stock in its estranged U.S. partner USAIr Group Inc.
Finance director Derek Stevens said BA was paid $17.3 million in June which helped offset a fall in the group's first-half operating profits announced earlier today.
But USAir paid a further $17.8 million last month which will appear in the third-quarter results, he told Reuters.
USAir still owes BA $23 million from deferred payments in the last two years.

Incensed by BA's plans to link up with American Airlines, USAir is suing its British partner in the U.S. federal court and has declared that it will end its code-sharing pact and frequent flier programme connection at the end of March.

BA said today it will continue to try and persuade USAir that it has a part to play in a triple alliance with American but believes it can continue to benefit from connections with USAir even if the east coast domestic carrier does break off the code-sharing partnership.
"We do not anticipate a sudden or significant reduction in feed onto our transatlantic services," chairman Sir Colin Marshall said in his results statement.
"We continue to be the principal international carrier serving USAir's hubs and travellers with USAir will still choose to fly British Airways across the Atlantic."

"You can sell seats by code-sharing but it is not the only way to sell seats," chief executive Robert Ayling later told a news conference. "The advantage we have is we have a lot of notice of the intention to end the arrangement."
BA has said the code-sharing and operational alliance with USAir generates about 70 million stg a year in additional operating profits for the British carrier.
"We do not stand to lose 70 million stg," Ayling said on Tuesday. "We stand to face a challenge which I am sure we will meet."
